titulo: Does setting the AC to 60 cool your house faster?
fuentes: ENERGY STAR (energystar.gov, Ask the Experts: variable speed room air conditioners): a conventional single-speed air conditioner is 'on' at maximum capacity when the thermostat calls for cooling and 'off' when the desired temperature has been achieved

frases.texto: You walk into a hot house and set the AC to sixty, so it cools off faster.
frases.estilo: Casual, like catching you in the act.

frases.texto: Here's the catch: with a basic air conditioner, sixty won't cool it any faster than a normal setting.
frases.estilo: Dry and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: A thermostat isn't a gas pedal. It's a destination.
A basic air conditioner runs at full blast whenever the thermostat calls for cooling, no matter how low you set it.
Then it shuts off once it reaches the temperature you set.
So a lower number only changes where it stops, not how fast it gets there.
Heads up: if a window is open or the sun is blasting in, no number will get you there.
Set it to a normal, comfortable temperature, and close the blinds.
Send this to the friend who sets the AC to sixty and waits.
frases.estilo: Playful, with humor, rhymes with the start.
